draft.title: Combustion and carbon stores
card: A carbon store is a place where carbon stays for a long time. Fossil fuels, rocks, oceans and forests are all carbon stores.
Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas formed from the remains of living things buried over millions of years. Their carbon has been locked away for that whole time.
Combustion means burning. When fossil fuels burn, the carbon in them joins with oxygen and is released into the air as carbon dioxide.
Nature moves carbon out of these stores slowly. Burning fuels releases it in a short time, so carbon dioxide can build up in the air.
draft.remember: Carbon can stay in stores for millions of years, but burning fossil fuels empties one store quickly.

a.q: What happens to the carbon in coal when a power station burns it?
opts: It is released into the air as carbon dioxide
It is stored deeper in the rocks as new coal
It is taken in by plants as carbon dioxide
It is turned into oxygen that stays in the air
a.why: Combustion joins the carbon in coal with oxygen, which makes carbon dioxide that goes into the air. It does not return to the rocks, because new coal takes millions of years to form.

b.q: Why can burning fossil fuels raise the amount of carbon dioxide in the air faster than natural processes remove it?
opts: It frees carbon stored for millions of years in a short time
It makes new carbon that was not on Earth before
It stops forests and oceans from taking in any carbon
It moves carbon from the air into rocks more quickly
b.why: Fossil fuels hold carbon that built up over millions of years, and burning releases it in a short time. Burning does not create carbon. It only moves carbon from one store to the air.
b.clue: Think about how long the carbon was stored and how long it takes to burn.

a.best: It is released into the air as carbon dioxide

b.best: It frees carbon stored for millions of years in a short time

problems.detail: "Empties one store quickly" overstates the card, which says burning "releases it in a short time". A student could read it as the whole fossil fuel store being emptied. "Releases carbon from one store quickly" would match the card.

The why says burning "only moves carbon from one store to the air". The claim is accurate, but it uses "only" where the card speaks of carbon dioxide that "can" build up. Rewording as "it moves carbon..." would avoid the absolute.
